column2: Being close by, I took the receiver from Mr. Kobayashi and held it to my ear.
Sure enough, I couldn't hear that dial tone, the “beeeep.”
I tapped the hook switch repeatedly, but nothing changed.
“Huh?”
I thought I heard something.
“What is it?”
“No, I thought I heard something...”
In the next moment, my spine froze.
A voice, as if rising from the bottom of a terribly deep well, was definitely echoing from the receiver.
It seemed to be calling someone.
It was neither a man's nor a woman's voice, but one clearly filled with sorrow and rage.
I dropped the receiver and looked up at the second floor...
at the ceiling.
What on earth was going on?
Just then, from that very second floor, I heard a woman's voice crying “Stop it!” along with an unintelligible scream.
I ran back up the stairs I had just come down.
There was no one in the hallway.
But the sounds of a struggle echoed from somewhere.
Which room could it be...?
Mr. Kayama's room!
I threw myself at the door of Mr. Kayama's room and turned the knob.
The door opened easily...
And an unbelievable sight spread before me.
Mr. Kayama lay on the floor drenched in blood, with Haruko draped over him as if shielding him.
A naked woman stood blocking the way in front of the two of them.
White bare skin, jet-black hair reaching her waist, and a bright red spray of blood from her face to her chest...
The eyes that glared at me as I entered were unmistakably {n2}'s.
help me...”
Haruko's hoarse voice came from the floor, but I couldn't take my eyes off {n2}.
is that you, {n2}?”
A gaping slit ran across her blood-covered face.
The voice that came from it was exactly like the voice on the phone earlier.
I crept closer.
With a whoosh, her long hair flashed like a whip.
Pain shot across my chest.
Startled, I looked down: my skin had been sliced in a straight line right through my sweater, blood seeping out.
“With her hair...?!”
Was this the true identity of whatever had killed Mr. Tanaka?
“Look out!”
Someone shouted, and I was shoved in the back.
A snake-like strand of hair grazed past my eyes as I fell.
Someone was covering me from behind.
It was Mr. Mikimoto.
If he hadn't shielded me, my throat would have been slit.
you're {n2}, aren't you?”
“No!
That's not...”
Mr. Mikimoto began to say.
“...Miyuki?
Is that you, Miyuki?”
Mr. Kobayashi stood in the doorway, dazed.
“Give back...
give back
my daughter...”
A sad and terrifying calling voice could be heard.
Could this...
could this be the ghost of {n2}'s mother?
I had always thought ghosts were more wispy and elusive...
“The body probably belongs to {n2}.”
As if reading my mind, Mr. Mikimoto whispered beside me.
“The body...
“That's right.
Her real mother, Miyuki, is just borrowing {n2}'s body.”
“Then...
then that's still {n2}?”
Just as Mr. Mikimoto was about to answer, the long hair stretched out and coiled around Mr. Kobayashi's throat with a hiss.
“Ugh...
h-
help...”
Mr. Kobayashi's face twisted in agony and swiftly turned purple.
“Stop it, {n2}!
Are you going to kill your uncle?!”
I shouted in despair.
The blood-soaked woman stopped moving.
...No, she was moving slightly.
Her face trembled, and now and then she twisted her body as if in pain.
As I watched, holding my breath, she suddenly crumpled.
Lying on the floor, her hair now reached only her shoulders, and Mr. Kobayashi sat on the floor with a blank look, clutching his throat.
I quietly approached her where she lay.
Was it {n2}?
Was she really {n2}?
“Get me a blanket!”
Mr. Mikimoto glanced at Mr. Kobayashi, still limp with shock, and said to me.
I hurriedly tore a blanket off the nearest bed and handed it to Mr. Mikimoto.
He wrapped the naked {n2} in it and lifted her up with ease.
“Somebody, please tend to these people.”
When Mr. Mikimoto pointed at the fallen Kayamas, Midori and Toshio, who had been outside, finally came in timidly.
Even so, never mind Haruko, Mr. Kayama was probably beyond help.
He didn't move a muscle, and judging by the amount of blood around, he wasn't likely to survive.
And to me, more than any of that, {n2} was what worried me far more.
Following Mr. Mikimoto, we carried {n2} to her room.
Going inside, we laid {n2} on the bed.
I looked around in case there was another, real {n2}, but of course there wasn't.
“Yes?”
“You're her boyfriend, aren't you?”
Mr. Mikimoto suddenly threw that question at me.
well, yes.”
It felt strange to deny it, so I answered that way.
“Then I'll leave the rest to you.”
“Leave it to me...
what am I supposed to do?
What if she turns into what she was just now?”
“I believe the evil spirit has gone for now, but...{r}{p}if you're worried, I'll give you this.”
What he handed me was something like a pendant.

It had originally seemed to be just a cross on a chain, but all sorts of things dangled from it: a charm from some shrine,{p} a carved wooden face like a Moai that looked like some kind of evil-warding talisman,{p} an animal fang, a blue stone, and so on
“What's this?”
I asked, half dumbfounded, and he answered with a perfectly straight face.
“Well.
I prepared it in case something like this happened.{r}{p}With evil spirits, who knows what works?{r}{p}With this much stuff, something's bound to protect you.”
I began to suspect he might be a rather sloppy sort of guy.
What's more, on closer look, the charm said “Prayer for Safe Childbirth.”
I wondered if I could really rely on a man like this, but right now there was nothing else to do.
I reconsidered: at least this man had initiative and a cool head. I hung the chain around my neck.
After Mr. Mikimoto left, I timidly approached the bed and looked down at {n2}.
Seeing the blood spray on her face beginning to harden, I thought I'd wipe it off.
When I went into the bathroom, I was again enveloped by the smell of blood.
Spots of blood were scattered on the bathtub and curtain.
Whose was it...?
I realized at once and was stunned.
This is Mr. Tanaka's blood!
{n2}, controlled by her mother, had killed Mr. Tanaka naked and then washed off the spattered blood in the shower!
Afterward {n2} had talked with me as if nothing had happened...
Sensing a presence, I turned around and {n2} was standing behind me.
Before I could scream, hair wrapped around my neck.
Would she slit my throat...?
Strangle me...?
The instant I thought that, a scream that didn't sound human rang out, and the hair coiled around me burst into flames like a fuse.
Could it be that this charm worked?
{n2}, her face contorted like a demoness, brushed away the sparks flying from her burning hair with both hands and staggered back two or three steps.
Come to your senses!”
Just as I shouted that, Mr. Mikimoto and Mr. Kobayashi burst in through the door.
“Are you all right?!”
The air, full of rage and curses, prickled against my skin.
Suddenly a whirlwind rose from beneath {n2}'s feet, gaining strength and circling around her.
All of us were slammed against the wall, unable to move.
{n2}, standing at the center of that mini-typhoon, rose gradually, spreading her arms with her head nearly touching the ceiling.
“I won't forgive...”
The window glass burst with a crash, but even the blizzard outside couldn't invade the storm inside the room.
“Murderer...”
The cover of the fluorescent light shattered, and fragments of plastic rained down, carried by the wind.
“Aaagh!”
Mr. Kobayashi groaned and clutched his leg.
Several shards of glass were stuck in his thigh.
Dark blood quickly spread across his trousers.
“Why did you kill...”
“Th-
that was a mistake!{r}{p}I only took the severance money because my father asked me to!{r}{p}If they hadn't made a scene, it never would have turned out like that!{r}{p}It wasn't my fault!”
Mr. Kobayashi began to scream this, spraying foam from his mouth.
“Severance money”...
“It wasn't my fault,” he says?
“You killed them?”
In the middle of that terrible gale, Mr. Mikimoto said it with astonishing calm.
“It wasn't my fault...”
Mr. Kobayashi, clutching his head with both hands, rubbed it against the floor as if prostrating himself.
“It wasn't my fault...
it wasn't my fault...”
Trembling, he kept repeating the same words.
More than the demoness-like {n2}, more than the unscientific phenomenon beyond common sense, what shocked me most was that Mr. Kobayashi was the one who had killed {n2}'s mother.
Suddenly I realized that the mini-typhoon from before had stopped dead.
The blizzard outside had calmed too, and the room was filled with a terrifying silence.
I forgot to breathe, staring at Mr. Kobayashi.
Breaking that silence, that voice rang out again.
“I won't forgive...”
Mr. Kobayashi looked up, startled, his face hideously twisted with fear, and saw {n2} floating above.
“I will never forgive you!”{g}
At that moment, {n2}'s whole body seemed to burst into pale blue flames.
{n2}'s hair, wreathed in pale blue flame, stretched hissing toward the neck of Mr. Kobayashi, who had collapsed to the floor.
Mr. Kobayashi stared at the hair as if mesmerized, unable to move.
“{n1}! The charm! Throw the charm at her!”
Mr. Mikimoto shouted.
I hurriedly tried to take the chain from my neck, but it caught and wouldn't come off.
The moment I pulled with all my strength, the chain snapped and all the charms scattered across the floor.
“Hurry!”
The hair wrapped around Mr. Kobayashi's neck, little by little trying to draw him toward {n2}.
Mr. Kobayashi rose, face twisted in agony, and soon was standing on tiptoe.
help...”
I frantically searched the charms scattered over the floor.
Cross,
Moai statue,
beast fang,
childbirth charm,
blue bead... I had no idea which one had been effective.
The cross and the childbirth charm lay closest at hand.
I picked up the childbirth charm and threw it at {n2}.
But the charm was too light and lost momentum midway, falling uselessly to the floor.
Next I threw the cross.
But the cross merely touched the pale blue flames wrapped around her, burst into fire, and fell as black dregs.
I picked up the cross and threw it at {n2}.
But the cross merely touched the pale blue flames wrapped around her, burst into fire, and fell as black dregs.
It's no use.
So it wasn't the cross that had worked.
Or had her power grown even stronger than before?
In despair, I picked up whatever charms lay on the floor and threw them one after another.
The beast fang,
the wooden statue,
the blue bead...
Nothing worked.
Mr. Kobayashi, hoisted into the air, kicked his legs.
“Stop it!”
Mr. Mikimoto shouted.
But Mr. Kobayashi twitched once and then hung limp like a puppet whose strings had been cut.
“Stop it...
please stop now, Sister!”
Such an utterly unexpected word left me staring blankly at Mr. Mikimoto.
Mr. Mikimoto stood and kept shouting at {n2} floating in the air.
“It's me,
Yosuke.{r}{p}Sister,
you're my sister Miyuki, aren't you?”
“Yosuke...”
Without taking my eyes off Mr. Mikimoto and {n2}, I kept groping the floor for anything left to throw.
Mr. Mikimoto was...
her brother?
Something touched my fingers, and when I picked it up it was the childbirth charm.
Damn, this is useless!
I cursed and slammed it to the floor, then searched for other charms.
Mr. Mikimoto kept talking.
“I happened to be at my aunt's house and escaped the disaster.{r}{p}I was still small back then, so nobody told me what had happened.{r}{p}I only learned the details after graduating from high school
.{r}{p}And that everyone in the village knew who the culprit was and pretended not to.{r}{p}The police did too.{r}{p}I made up my mind.
I would take revenge with my own hands.”
Mr. Kobayashi's body dropped to the floor with a thud.
Seeing him not move a muscle, he might already be dead...
Mr. Mikimoto ran over and checked his pulse.
“Take revenge...
take revenge for us...”
Mr. Mikimoto shook his head.
“I didn't intend to kill him.
I only wanted to bring out the truth.{r}{p}Legally, the statute of limitations has run out too.”
I won't allow that!”
It was as if the room, no, the entire building, was shouting in anger.
The floor creaked, the walls bulged, the ceiling shook.
“I'll kill you all!”
“Stop it, Sister!
...Whoa!”
Cracks ran through the ceiling right above Mr. Mikimoto and Mr. Kobayashi, and splinters of wood rained down.
The charm!
Hurry!”
“But none of them work!”
I shouted back at the top of my voice so as not to be drowned out by the gale rising strong again.
“Idiot!
The one right there!
That's the charm my sister Miyuki was holding when {n2} was born!”
The charm from when {n2} was born...
So that was it.
The charm she'd prayed over for a safe birth in her happy days.
That very charm held the power to blow away an evil spirit consumed by vengeance.
As I reached for the charm on the floor, the wooden floor rippled like a living thing and sent the charm flying to the other side of the room.
I stood and ran for the charm.
{n2}'s hair twined around my neck and nearly hoisted me into the air.
I hurriedly jammed my fingers in, but my throat was crushed and I couldn't even groan.
“Stop it, Sister!
If you wish for {n2}'s happiness, stop now!”
For an instant the grip loosened.
Prying with my fingers I slipped my head free and rolled across the floor to dive for the charm.
Almost the instant I picked it up, pale blue flames shot from {n2}'s body toward me.
Closing my eyes, I held the charm up before my face.
I braced for intense heat or impact, but felt nothing.
Timidly opening my eyes, I saw the childbirth charm catching the pale blue flames.
Or rather, the flames were shrinking rapidly just before the charm and vanishing.
Summoning my courage, I stood and approached {n2} with the charm held high.
As if the charm were sucking away their vitality, the pale blue flames faded and {n2}'s body lowered little by little.
my daughter...”
“She's not only your daughter!
She's the daughter of my brother-in-law Ichiro and you!”
Mr. Mikimoto cried out in anguish, tears streaming.
{n2}'s body jerked in midair.
“...Ichiro...”
Staggering, I moved still closer to her.
Her blood-covered chest was at eye level.
Her face looked up at the ceiling, still rolled back to the whites of her eyes.
The evil spirit...
no, Miyuki's spirit had now clearly lost its malice.
But I didn't know what I should do, and stood fretting, clutching the charm.
I called out the most precious name.
Calling her name seemed to snap the hoop of reason in my head.
Thinking of nothing, I hugged her floating body with all my might.
The moment our bodies touched, there was a dazzling light and an explosive shock that nearly blew me away.
I wrapped both arms firmly around her back and clung on desperately.
The charm in my hand grew too hot to hold, but I gritted my teeth and endured.
“Nooooo!”{g}
A voice that was neither {n2}'s nor her mother's echoed through the room.
“Give {n2}...
give {n2} back!”
I cried at the top of my voice.
In the next moment, {n2}'s entire weight, which had been floating in the air, bore down on me, and I staggered and fell backward.
{n2}'s body was limp, motionless as if dead, and terribly heavy.
The last of the pale blue flames that had faintly wrapped {n2} left her and drifted vaguely in the air.
For an instant it seemed to take human form, but when I blinked and looked hard, there was nothing there.
“Sister...”
Looking at Mr. Mikimoto, I saw him staring at the same spot as me, tears streaming.
“...Has she...
gone now?”
I asked, and he nodded firmly.
“She's gone.
I can tell.{r}{p}...She won't be coming back.”
The vibrations of the building and the strange wind were all silent, as if they'd been illusions.
Even outside the window it was so quiet you could almost hear the snow piling up.
“Mr. Kobayashi...
is he...”
“He's all right.
Only unconscious.”
Mr. Mikimoto lifted {n2}'s body, carried her to the bed, and covered her with a blanket.
I stood up unsteadily and looked at her face.
“How on earth did this happen?{r}{p}Why did you in the first place...?”

“I had kept searching for evidence that someone in the Kobayashi family was the culprit.{r}{p}At some point, I caught wind of a rumor that this inn is haunted in winter.{r}{p}I was half skeptical, but even if it was only a rumor,
I thought that if I poked at it right, I might draw out a confession from fear and guilt.”
“But telling that story with {n2} present was a mistake after all.{r}{p}Most likely, {n2}, in shock, synchronized with my sister's residual thoughts
.{r}{p}Maybe {n2} herself fiercely hated her uncle and grandfather too.”
“In any case, what had been a mere troublemaking ghost until then turned into a terrible demon.”
“Does {n2}...
does {n2} remember?
What happened until a moment ago?”
If so, it's unbearable.
She'd killed two people and nearly killed her own uncle.
If she'd watched all of that from inside a body taken over by her mother...
Mr. Mikimoto shook his head.
“I don't know.
If she did watch, she'll have suffered an unimaginable shock.{r}{p}She might not be able to recover at all...
on her own.”
He turned toward me.
“You're the only one who can help her.
Take care of her.”
I nodded, but I had no confidence at all.
Still...
looking down at {n2}, her face gaunt after such a short time, I thought.
All I can do is do what I can.
I tried to take {n2}'s hand and realized I was still gripping that charm tightly.
I was gripping it so hard I had to pry my stiff fingers open.
I pressed the charm into her hand, wrapped it with both of mine, and closed my eyes.
